He played [[college basketball]] for the [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU Horned Frogs]]. Noi started his professional career in 2019 with the [[Cairns Taipans]] of the NBL. He joined the [[Sydney Kings]] in 2022 and won [[List of NBL champions|NBL championships]] in 2023 and 2026. == Early life == Noi was born in [[Khartoum]], Sudan,{{cite web |title=Australia – 2014 FIBA Under-17 World Championship |url=http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/team/p/sid/6224/tid/239/_/2014_FIBA_U17_World_Championship_for_Men/index.html |website=fiba.com |access-date=8 March 2025 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906054031/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/team/p/sid/6224/tid/239/_/2014_FIBA_U17_World_Championship_for_Men/index.html |archive-date=6 September 2015}} during the height of the [[Second Sudanese Civil War]]. His family fled the country amid escalations of the conflict, first to Egypt and later to Australia in 2002.{{cite web|title=TCU's Noi Goes from Fleeing South Sudan to College Basketball Success|url=https://www.nbcdfw.com/news/sports/TCUs-Noi-Goes-from-Fleeing-South-Sudan-to-College-Basketball-Success-505163591.html|website=NBSDFW.com|date=31 January 2019}} Growing up in [[Newcastle, New South Wales|Newcastle]], he blossomed into a basketball star, and went on to average 9.1 points and 4.3 rebounds while helping lead Australia to a silver medal at the [[2014 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] in [[Dubai]].{{cite web|work=FIBA.basketball|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2014/player/Kouat-Noi|title=Kouat Noi|accessdate=31 January 2019}} Noi attended [[San Clemente High School (Mayfield, New South Wales)|San Clemente High School]]{{cite web |last1=Kerry |first1=Craig |title=Hunters teen gets national call-up |url=https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/1514962/hunters-teen-gets-national-call-up/ |website=Newcastle Herald |access-date=12 March 2024 |date=20 May 2013 |quote=A San Clemente High School student, Noi was named in a 20-man Australian squad after representing NSW Country at the national under-16... |url-access=subscription}} and [[St Francis Xavier's College, Hamilton|St Francis Xavier's College]] in Newcastle.{{cite web |last1=Keeble |first1=Brett |title=Newcastle's Kouat Noi, out of Africa and bound for the US |url=https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/2551848/newcastles-kouat-noi-out-of-africa-and-bound-for-the-us/ |website=Newcastle Herald |access-date=7 November 2021 |date=10 September 2014}} In 2014, Noi moved to the United States and enrolled at [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]], where he briefly played alongside [[Ben Simmons]].{{cite web|title=Newcastle's Kouat Noi, out of Africa and bound for the US|url=https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/2551848/newcastles-kouat-noi-out-of-africa-and-bound-for-the-us/|website=Newcastle Herald|date=10 September 2014}} As a senior in the 2015–16 season, Noi averaged more than 19 points per game for the Eagles.{{cite web|title=TCU announces addition of Noi|url=https://gofrogs.com/news/2016/8/22/TCU_Announces_Addition_of_Noi_Monday_Afternoon.aspx|website=GoFrogs.com|date=22 August 2016}} == College career == Noi enrolled at [[Texas Christian University]] (TCU) on a basketball scholarship in the summer of 2016, and redshirted in his first season on campus as the [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|Horned Frogs]] won the [[2017 National Invitation Tournament|2017 NIT]] title{{cite web|title=TCU uses fast start to rout Georgia Tech, captures first NIT title|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400949062|website=ESPN.com|date=30 March 2017}} under first-year head coach [[Jamie Dixon]]. In 2017–18, Noi played in all 33 of TCU's games, starting nine of them. He averaged 10.2 points per game as the Frogs finished the season with a 21-12 record and secured a berth in the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA tournament]], the program's first in 20 years.{{cite web|title=A Record 7 Texas Teams Are In The NCAA Tournament|url=https://www.keranews.org/post/record-7-texas-teams-are-ncaa-tournament-here-s-when-catch-them|website=KERA News|date=12 March 2018|access-date=3 February 2019|archive-date=27 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190127094115/https://www.keranews.org/post/record-7-texas-teams-are-ncaa-tournament-here-s-when-catch-them|url-status=dead}} As a sophomore, Noi registered his first collegiate 20-point game with a 27-point performance against [[Eastern Michigan Eagles men's basketball|Eastern Michigan]] on 26 November 2018{{cite web|title=Frogs Down Eagles, 87-69|url=https://gofrogs.com/news/2018/11/26/mens-basketball-frogs-down-eagles-87-69.aspx|website=GoFrogs.com|date=26 November 2018}} and his first career 30-point game against [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]] on 12 January 2019.{{cite web|title=Noi scores 30, Frogs fall to Sooners|url=https://gofrogs.com/news/2019/1/12/mens-basketball-noi-scores-30-frogs-fall-to-sooners.aspx|website=GoFrogs.com|date=January 12, 2019}} Noi averaged 13.9 points and 4.9 rebounds per game as a sophomore playing in 31 games, including 19 starts. He declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]], forfeiting his remaining two years of eligibility.{{cite news|last1=Davison|first1=Drew|title='It's my time.' TCU's Kouat Noi is 'all-in' pursuing NBA, professional dreams|url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-christian-university/article229145374.html|work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]|accessdate=12 April 2019|date=11 April 2019}} He later withdrew from the draft.{{cite web|last1=Triebwasser|first1=Melissa B.|title=Kouat Noi withdraws from the NBA Draft|url=https://www.frogsowar.com/2019/6/13/18677762/kouat-noi-withdraws-from-the-nba-draft|website=Frogs o' War|publisher=SB Nation|accessdate=27 July 2019|date=13 June 2019}} ==Professional career== === Cairns Taipans (2019–2022) === [[File:NBL20 PS - CNS v BNE 15.9.19 - 12 (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Noi shoots a lay-up against the [[Brisbane Bullets]] during a 2019 pre-season game|150px]] In July 2019, Noi signed with the [[Cairns Taipans]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]].{{cite web |title=Former Frog Kouat Noi signs with Cairns Taipans |url=https://www.frogsowar.com/2019/7/4/20681966/former-frog-kouat-noi-signs-with-cairns-taipans |website=Frogs O'War |accessdate=2 December 2019 |date=4 July 2019}} In March 2021, he suffered a [[Posterior cruciate ligament|PCL]] injury that ruled him out for 12 weeks.{{cite web |title=Injury News: Kouat Noi |url=https://www.taipans.com/news/injury-news-kouat-noi |website=Taipans.com |accessdate=27 March 2021 |date=26 March 2021}} He re-signed with the Taipans in June 2021.{{cite web |title=The sssssilent star |url=https://twitter.com/CairnsTaipans/status/1408666767522623489 |website=twitter.com/CairnsTaipans |access-date=12 May 2022 |date=25 June 2021}} === Sydney Kings and off-season stints (2022–2026) === Following the [[2021–22 NBL season]], Noi joined the [[USC Rip City]] of the [[NBL1 North]] for the [[2022 NBL1 season|2022 season]], where he earned league MVP and All-Star Five honours.{{cite web |title=Congratulations to Kouat Noi (University of Sunshine Coast Basketball Club) on taking home the NBL1 North Men's Most Valuable Player Award |url=https://www.facebook.com/basketballqld/posts/pfbid0355ekVYYxoht7jC25YVQQ5DgoQNubsEA7ewR43KtEGLs21ZwECmc37s67T7HYWFkcl |website=facebook.com/basketballqld |access-date=10 August 2022 |date=10 August 2022}}{{cite web |title=Congratulations to the NBL1 North Men's All Star Five |url=https://www.facebook.com/basketballqld/posts/pfbid0yBVodosDerrtW1Y4XENZhWuPRRTDDgfvyyvthw2WqJzzwErVagcV8GLBwicTVFNNl |website=facebook.com/basketballqld |access-date=10 August 2022 |date=10 August 2022}} In June 2022, Noi signed a two-year contract with the [[Sydney Kings]].{{Cite web|title=Kouat Noi signs on for two years with the Sydney Kings|url=https://www.sydneykings.com/news/kouat-noi-signs-on-for-two-years-with-the-sydney-kings|website=SydneyKings.com|date=6 June 2022|access-date=6 June 2022}} After winning the 2022–23 championship, the club exercised its team option on his contract.{{Cite web|title=Noi Aims to Continue Kings' Reign|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/noi-aims-to-continue-kings-reign|website=NBL.com.au|date=25 March 2023|access-date=25 March 2023}} Noi re-joined the USC Rip City for the [[2023 NBL1 season|2023 NBL1 North season]].{{Cite web|title=King of the north Noi returns to Rip City|url=https://www.sydneykings.com/news/king-of-the-north-noi-returns-to-rip-city|website=sydneykings.com|date=30 April 2023|access-date=4 May 2023}}{{Cite web|title=Noi makes NBL1 season debut as Rip City fall to Northside|url=https://www.sydneykings.com/news/noi-makes-nbl1-season-debut-as-rip-city-fall-to-northside|website=sydneykings.com|date=1 May 2023|access-date=4 May 2023}} He was named to the All-NBL1 North First Team for the second straight year.{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/basketballqld/posts/pfbid0GVYpDCDV2ZndbZDyWohw51UYnH2TMMM18UJ6h4c8WyYZJo2s6sN46wxMgE9ZXBSml|title=NBL1 North First & Second Team | Men's|work=facebook.com/basketballqld|date=17 July 2023|access-date=17 July 2023}} In the [[2023–24 NBL season]], Noi averaged 10.0 points and 4.5 rebounds in 25 games for the Kings.{{cite web |title=Kouat Noi |url=https://nbl.com.au/player/3694/1279435/kouat-noi |website=NBL.com.au |access-date=6 April 2025}} On 18 March 2024, Noi signed with the [[Darwin Salties]] for the [[2024 NBL1 season|2024 NBL1 North season]].{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/darwinsalties/posts/pfbid02nB4DUwZNnBUx7GwrLUusfBB4q5vWXqNK8m6PEPnHBrRoVFrKe3R5QKkbLDP8B1Vol|title=The Tamboran Darwin SALTIES have secured a major coup by signing NBL champion Kouat Noi for the upcoming 2024 NBL1 season...|website=facebook.com/darwinsalties|date=18 March 2024|access-date=19 March 2024}}{{cite web|title=NBL1 North superstar signs with Darwin|url=https://nbl1.com.au/news/nbl1-north-superstar-signs-with-darwin|website=NBL1.com.au|access-date=19 March 2024|date=18 March 2024}} He was named to the NBL1 North First Team for the third straight year.{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/basketballqld/posts/pfbid02NzraRKAxeqA1V6v1jigiv55z1r2HxFnMMW1dfkENFwhTHMWD2DQnNtrxxJvX8Hb6l|title=NBL1 North Men's First Team|work=facebook.com/basketballqld|date=15 July 2024|access-date=15 July 2024}} On 2 April 2024, Noi re-signed with the Kings on a three-year deal.{{Cite web|title=King Kouat inks three-year deal with Sydney|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/king-kouat-inks-three-year-deal-with-sydney|website=NBL.com.au|date=2 April 2024|access-date=2 April 2024}} On 19 January 2025, he scored a career-high 32 points in an 88–77 win over the [[Tasmania JackJumpers]].{{cite news |title=Noi the difference in crucial Kings win |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/noi-the-difference-in-crucial-kings-win |access-date=19 January 2025 |work=NBL Official Website |date=19 January 2025}} He was named the [[NBL Best Sixth Man Award|NBL Best Sixth Man]] for the [[2024–25 NBL season|2024–25 season]].{{cite news |title=Cotton wins 5th MVP |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/cotton-wins-5th-mvp |access-date=10 February 2025 |work=NBL Official Website |date=10 February 2025}} On 27 February 2025, Noi signed with the [[Ningbo Rockets]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA) for the rest of the 2024–25 season.{{cite web |title=NBL最佳第六人！宁波官方：球队已和外籍球员库阿特-诺伊完成签约 |url=https://news.zhibo8.com/nba/2025-02-27/67c035b403ebenative.htm |website=直播吧 |access-date=2 March 2025 |date=27 February 2025}} Following the CBA season, he joined the Sutherland Sharks of the [[NBL1 East]] for the [[2025 NBL1 season|2025 season]].{{cite news |title=Sutherland sign NBL star Kouat Noi |url=https://nbl1.com.au/news/sutherland-sign-nbl-star-kouat-noi |access-date=7 April 2025 |work=nbl1.com.au |date=7 April 2025 |language=en}} In the [[2025–26 NBL season]], Noi won his second NBL championship with the Kings. He parted ways with the Kings following the season after 127 games across four seasons.{{cite news |last1=Shadlow |first1=Jai |title=BREAKING: Signing spree continues as emerging NBL force snaps up two-time champ |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/nbl-free-agency-new-zealand-breakers-sign-nbl-champion-kouat-noi-from-sydney-kings-latest-news-and-player-moves/news-story/41afe78fb726c769ef76b5e46399e309 |access-date=18 May 2026 |work=Fox Sports |date=18 May 2026 |language=en}} In May 2026, Noi joined [[Al Riyadi Club Beirut|Al Riyadi]] for the end of the 2025–26 [[Lebanese Basketball League]] season.{{cite web |title=Kouat Noi |url=https://basketball.asia-basket.com/player/Kouat-Noi/333019 |website=Eurobasket |access-date=4 August 2026 |url-access=subscription}} He helped the team win the championship, averaging 13.6 points per game across the seven-game Finals series.{{cite news |title=Team-by-Team: NBL26/27 Off-Season Wrap |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/nbl26-27-off-season-wrap-team-by-team-best-performances |access-date=4 August 2026 |work=nbl.com.au |date=4 August 2026 |language=en}} ===New Zealand Breakers (2026–present)=== On 22 May 2026, Noi signed a two-year deal with the [[New Zealand Breakers]].{{cite news |title=Two-time champion joins New Zealand |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/two-time-champion-kouat-noi-signs-with-new-zealand-breakers |access-date=22 May 2026 |work=nbl.com.au |date=22 May 2026 |language=en}} ==National team career== Noi was named to the training camp squad of the [[South Sudan men's national basketball team|South Sudan basketball team]] for the [[2024 Summer Olympics]].{{cite web |title=South Sudan names NBL-laden Olympic squad |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/south-sudan-names-nbl-laden-olympic-squad |website=NBL |access-date=15 July 2024 |date=30 April 2024}} ==Personal life== Noi was born in Sudan but considers himself as South Sudanese.{{cite web |last1=Olivieri |first1=Anthony |title=Fleeing violence in Sudan, TCU's Kouat Noi found a home in Australia |url=https://www.espn.com.au/espn/story/_/id/25998162/tcu-forward-kouat-noi-fled-violence-sudan-home-australia-cbb |website=ESPN |access-date=7 November 2021 |date=15 February 2019}} His father, Ater Dhiu, played basketball for the [[Sudan men's national basketball team]].{{cite web |last1=Keeble |first1=Brett |title=Noi's Aussie hoop dream alive again |url=https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/1780991/nois-aussie-hoop-dream-alive-again/ |website=Newcastle Herald |access-date=7 November 2021 |date=16 September 2013}}{{cite web |last1=Kerry |first1=Craig |title=Long on ambition: Teenager reaches NSW Country start |url=https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/116350/long-on-ambition-teenager-reaches-nsw-country-start/ |website=Newcastle Herald |access-date=7 November 2021 |date=21 May 2012}} Noi is a cousin of fellow basketball players, [[Yuat Alok]] and [[Lat Mayen]].{{cite web|last=Olivieri|first=Anthony|url=https://www.espn.com.au/espn/story/_/id/25998162/tcu-forward-kouat-noi-fled-violence-sudan-home-australia-cbb|title=Fleeing violence in Sudan, TCU's Kouat Noi found B.|url=https://www.frogsowar.com/2019/7/11/20690712/lat-mayen-has-left-tcu-basketball|title=Lat Mayen has left TCU Basketball|work=frogsowar.com|date=11 July 2019|access-date=26 January 2024}} Noi has
